q1.feedback: It can feel that way. But the memory of asking has faded, so this really is the first time for her.
Possible, but usually not. Even when she heard you clearly, the answer may not stay.
Exactly. That’s why the worry is what needs an answer.

q2.feedback: The time may not stay. The empty afternoon is the real issue here.
Yes. Boredom often drives the loop, and doing something together answers it.
Understandable when you’re tired, but she may feel brushed off, and that feeling lingers.

q3.feedback: Kind, but it brushes the feeling aside.
Yes. You named the feeling, gently.
That’s the fact. Useful, but the feeling comes first.

tf1.feedback: It feels like it should. But long explanations are hard to hold on to and can add to the worry.
Right. Short and the same each time works better than more detail.

q4.feedback: That gives the worry a whole week to grow.
Yes. Close to the time, and easy to see.
Surprises can be upsetting too. Close to the time works best.

recap.feedback: True, but it skips the feeling and points at the forgetting.
Yes: the feeling, a short reassurance, and something to do together.
Warm, but it brushes the feeling aside and offers nothing to do.

builder.text: We have plenty of time. I’ll tell you when.
Want to help me with the tea?
